nodes.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection whose double-point set is empty, then $L$ admits an alternating diagram.
nodes.title: Links with a crossing-free regular projection admit alternating diagrams

nodes.summary: A parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components admits an alternating diagram when there is a parametrized link $L'$ isotopic to $L$ whose standard projection is regular and alternating.
nodes.title: Links admitting an alternating diagram

nodes.summary: The number of components of a dart diagram $D$ is the number of classes of darts of $D$ under unoriented strand connectivity, plus the recorded number of isolated crossingless components of $D$.
nodes.title: Number of components of a dart diagram

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, this is the equivalence relation on the darts of $D$ generated by relating each dart $d$ to its partner across an edge segment and to the opposite dart of $d$ at the same crossing. Two darts are related exactly when they lie on the same unoriented strand component.
nodes.title: Strand-connectivity relation on darts

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ whose standard projection is regular, the crossing count of $L$ is the number of crossings of the projection, that is, the number of points of its double-point set.
nodes.title: Crossing count of a regular projection

nodes.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection whose double-point set is empty, then the crossing count of $L$ is $0$.
nodes.title: A crossing-free regular projection has crossing count zero

nodes.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection with at least one crossing, then the crossing count of $L$ is positive.
nodes.title: A regular projection with a crossing has positive crossing count

nodes.summary: The crossing count of a dart diagram $D$ is the number of vertices of $D$, each vertex being one crossing.
nodes.title: Number of crossings of a dart diagram

nodes.summary: If two parametrized links $L_1$ and $L_2$ with $n$ components are isotopic, then $L_1$ and $L_2$ have the same crossing number.
nodes.title: The crossing number is an isotopy invariant

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be parametrized links with $n$ components such that $L'$ is isotopic to $L$. If the standard projection of $L'$ is regular and its double-point set is empty, then the crossing number of $L$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Crossing number zero from a crossing-free representative

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be oriented labeled parametrized links with $n$ components, with $L'$ ambient isotopic to $L$, and suppose the standard projection of $L'$ to the plane is regular. Then the crossing number of $L$ is at most the number of crossings of this projection of $L'$.
nodes.title: Regular projections of isotopic links bound the crossing number

nodes.summary: If the standard projection of an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ to the plane is regular, then the crossing number of $L$ is at most the number of crossings of this projection.
nodes.title: A link's own regular projection bounds its crossing number

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be oriented labeled parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L'$ is ambient isotopic to $L$ and the standard projection of $L'$ to the plane is regular, then the crossing number of $L$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the crossing number

nodes.summary: For an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the crossing number of $L$ is the infimum in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, over all parametrized links $L'$ with $n$ components that are ambient isotopic to $L$ and whose standard projection to the plane is regular, of the number of crossings (double points) of that projection of $L'$. It is $\infty$ when no such $L'$ exists.
nodes.title: Crossing number of a link

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components. A crossing of $L$ is a point of the double-point set of $L$, that is, a point $p$ of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that two distinct parameter points of $L$ both have image $p$ under the standard projection forgetting the third coordinate.
nodes.title: Crossings of a link projection

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be an oriented labeled parametrized link, with each component parametrized by $t \in [0, 2\pi)$. Two distinct parameter points $a$ and $b$ of $L$ on the same component are cyclically adjacent, in this order, when both are crossing preimages (they project to double points of the standard projection) and no crossing preimage on that component lies in the open arc from $a$ to $b$ in the direction of increasing…
nodes.title: Cyclically adjacent crossing preimages

nodes.summary: A dart diagram consists of a finite set $V$ of crossings, a fixed-point-free involution $\mathrm{pair}$ of the set $V \times \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ of darts, and a natural number counting isolated crossingless components.
nodes.title: Dart diagram

nodes.summary: The darts of a dart diagram $D$ with crossing set $V$ are the pairs $(v, i)$ with $v \in V$ and $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$; the dart $(v, i)$ is the $i$-th incident half-edge at the crossing $v$.
nodes.title: Darts of a dart diagram

nodes.summary: For an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the double-point set of $L$ is the set of points $p$ of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ for which there are two distinct parameter points of $L$ (each a component index together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$) whose images under the standard projection, which forgets the third coordinate, both equal $p$.
nodes.title: Double points of a link projection

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the empty dart diagram with $k$ isolated components has no crossings, hence no darts, and records $k$ isolated crossingless components.
nodes.title: Empty dart diagram

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. Every parameter point of $L$ whose projected point is $p$ is either the over-strand preimage or the under-strand preimage of $p$.
nodes.title: The over and under preimages exhaust a crossing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a point of the double-point set of $L$. Then there are parameter points $a \ne b$ of $L$ whose projected points are both $p$, and every parameter point of $L$ whose projected point is $p$ is $a$ or $b$.
nodes.title: Double points have exactly two preimages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. There is exactly one parameter point $a$ of $L$ that is an over-strand preimage of $p$: the projected point of $a$ is $p$, and every other parameter point whose projected point is $p$ has height strictly less than the height of $a$.
nodes.title: The over-strand preimage exists and is unique

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. There is exactly one parameter point $a$ of $L$ that is an under-strand preimage of $p$: the projected point of $a$ is $p$, and every other parameter point whose projected point is $p$ has height strictly greater than the height of $a$.
nodes.title: The under-strand preimage exists and is unique

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components. If two distinct parameter points $a \ne b$ of $L$ have the same projected point, then the heights of $L$ at $a$ and at $b$ are different.
nodes.title: Points with the same projection have different heights

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. The height of $L$ at the under-strand preimage of $p$ is strictly less than its height at the over-strand preimage of $p$.
nodes.title: The under-strand lies strictly below the over-strand

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components and a parameter point $a$ of $L$, the height of $L$ at $a$ is the height (the third coordinate) of the point of Euclidean 3-space that $a$ represents on $L$.
nodes.title: Height of a parameter point

nodes.summary: The height of a point $x = (x_1, x_2, x_3)$ of Euclidean 3-space is its third coordinate $x_3$.
nodes.title: Height in the standard projection frame

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the union over all components $i$ of the images of the projected curves of $L$ equals the image of the trace of $L$ under the standard projection to the plane.
nodes.title: The projected trace is the union of the projected components

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be parameter points with parameters $s$, $u$, $t \in [0, 2\pi)$ respectively. Then $c$ lies in the open counterclockwise arc from $a$ to $b$ when $s < t < u$ in case $s < u$, and when $s < t$ or $t < u$ in case $u \le s$. Only the parameters are compared; the components of $a$, $b$, $c$ play no role.
nodes.title: Open arc on the parameter circle

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. If the double-point set of this projection is empty, then the projection is alternating.
nodes.title: Crossingless regular projections are alternating

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. The projection is alternating when, for any two cyclically adjacent crossing preimages $a$ and $b$ of $L$ (distinct, on the same component, with no other crossing preimage of that component in the open arc of parameters from $a$ to $b$), the over/under status at $a$ differs from the over/under status at $b$.
nodes.title: Alternating regular projections

nodes.summary: A dart diagram is alternating when, for every dart $d$, the dart $\operatorname{next}(d)$, reached from $d$ by crossing its edge segment and going straight through the next crossing, has the opposite over/under status to $d$. In other words, consecutive crossings on every strand have opposite over/under status.
nodes.title: Alternating dart diagrams

nodes.summary: A parameter point $a$ of a parametrized link $L$ (a component of $L$ together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$) is a crossing preimage when its image under the standard projection to the plane lies in the double-point set of $L$.
nodes.title: Crossing preimages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. If $a \ne b$ are crossing preimages of $L$ with the same projection, then the over/under status at $a$ differs from the over/under status at $b$.
nodes.title: The two preimages of a crossing have opposite status

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular, and let $a$ be a crossing preimage of $L$. The over/under status at $a$ is true when $a$ is the over-strand preimage of the crossing at the projection of $a$, that is, the preimage of that crossing of greatest height, and false otherwise.
nodes.title: Over/under status at a crossing preimage

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and $p$ a crossing of its standard projection to the plane. A parameter point $a$ of $L$ is an over point of $p$ when $a$ projects to $p$ and every other parameter point that projects to $p$ has strictly smaller height than $a$.
nodes.title: Being the over-strand preimage of a crossing

nodes.summary: The four darts at a crossing of a dart diagram carry the labels $0, 1, 2, 3$ in cyclic order. A dart lies on the over-strand at its crossing when its label is $0$ or $2$.
nodes.title: Over-strand darts

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link; a parameter point of $L$ is a component of $L$ together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$. The standard projection of $L$ to the plane, which forgets the third coordinate, is regular when the following hold: at every parameter point, the projection of the velocity vector of the component curve is nonzero; the double-point set is finite; no three pairwise distinct parameter points have…
nodes.title: Regular projections

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and $p$ a crossing of its standard projection to the plane. A parameter point $a$ of $L$ is an under point of $p$ when $a$ projects to $p$ and every other parameter point that projects to $p$ has strictly greater height than $a$.
nodes.title: Being the under-strand preimage of a crossing

nodes.summary: For every dart diagram $D$, the number of isolated crossingless components recorded in $D$ is at most the number of components of $D$.
nodes.title: Isolated components are counted in the component count

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the strand traversal permutation of the darts of $D$ is the edge-pairing permutation followed by the opposite-dart permutation: it sends a dart $d$ to the dart opposite $\mathrm{pair}(d)$ at its crossing, where $\mathrm{pair}$ is the edge-pairing involution of $D$.
nodes.title: Strand traversal permutation

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$ and a dart $d$ of $D$, the next dart after $d$ is the dart opposite $\mathrm{pair}(d)$ at its crossing, where $\mathrm{pair}$ is the edge-pairing involution of $D$: cross the edge segment at $d$, then go straight through the crossing reached.
nodes.title: Strand traversal step

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L_1$ is isotopic to $L_2$ and $L_1$ admits an alternating diagram, then $L_2$ admits an alternating diagram.
nodes.title: Admitting an alternating diagram is an isotopy invariant

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the opposite-dart permutation of the darts of $D$ is the square of the quarter-turn rotation permutation: it sends the dart $(v, i)$ at crossing $v$ to the dart $(v, i + 2)$, with labels taken modulo $4$.
nodes.title: Opposite-dart permutation

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$ and a dart $d = (v, i)$ of $D$, the opposite dart is obtained by rotating $d$ twice counterclockwise around its crossing $v$; it is the dart $(v, i + 2)$, with labels taken modulo $4$.
nodes.title: Opposite dart

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. The over-strand preimage of $p$ is the unique parameter point $a$ of $L$ that projects to $p$ and such that every other parameter point projecting to $p$ has strictly smaller height than $a$.
nodes.title: Over-strand preimage of a crossing

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the edge-pairing permutation is the edge-pairing involution of $D$ regarded as a permutation of the darts of $D$; it is its own inverse.
nodes.title: Edge-pairing permutation

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a parameter point consists of a component index $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a real parameter $t$ with $0 \le t < 2\pi$, the fundamental half-open period. It represents the point at parameter $t$ of component $i$ of a parametrized link with $n$ components.
nodes.title: Parameter point

nodes.summary: The standard projection sends a point $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2)$ of Euclidean 3-space to the point $(x_0, x_1)$ of the Euclidean plane, forgetting the third coordinate.
nodes.title: Standard projection to the plane

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a parameter point $a = (i, t)$, with $i < n$ and $t \in [0, 2\pi)$, the point of $L$ at $a$ is $\gamma_i(t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
nodes.title: Point of a link at a parameter point

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and $i < n$, the projected curve of component $i$ is the map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^2$, $t \mapsto \pi(\gamma_i(t))$, where $\pi(x_0, x_1, x_2) = (x_0, x_1)$ is the standard projection forgetting the third coordinate.
nodes.title: Projected curve of a link component

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of $L$, that is, a point of the double-point set of its projection. Then the projected point of the over-strand parameter point at $p$ is $p$.
nodes.title: The over-strand preimage lies over its crossing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of $L$, that is, a point of the double-point set of its projection. Then the projected point of the under-strand parameter point at $p$ is $p$.
nodes.title: The under-strand preimage lies over its crossing

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a parameter point $a = (i, t)$, with $i < n$ and $t \in [0, 2\pi)$, the projected point of $L$ at $a$ is $\pi(\gamma_i(t)) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, where $\pi(x_0, x_1, x_2) = (x_0, x_1)$ forgets the third coordinate.
nodes.title: Projected point of a link at a parameter point

nodes.summary: The space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with its Euclidean inner product and norm, the target plane of the fixed standard projection frame.
nodes.title: Euclidean plane

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the rotation permutation is the permutation of the darts of $D$ sending a dart $(v, i)$, with $v$ a crossing and $i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, to $(v, i + 1)$; its inverse sends $(v, i)$ to $(v, i - 1)$.
nodes.title: Rotation permutation of darts

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the rotation of a dart $(v, i)$ of $D$, with $v$ a crossing and $i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, is the dart $(v, i + 1)$: one step counterclockwise around the crossing $v$.
nodes.title: Rotation of a dart

nodes.summary: For every dart $d$ of a dart diagram $D$, the dart $\operatorname{next}(d)$ reached by one step of strand traversal lies in the same component as $d$.
nodes.title: A traversal step stays in the same component

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, two darts of $D$ lie in the same component when they are related by the equivalence relation on darts generated by $d \sim \operatorname{pair}(d)$, crossing an edge segment, and $d \sim \operatorname{opposite}(d)$, going straight through a crossing.
nodes.title: Same component relation on darts

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a dart diagram, and for a dart $d$ of $D$ let $\operatorname{next}(d)$ be the dart reached from $d$ by crossing its edge segment and then going straight through the next crossing. Then for every dart $d$ of $D$, the darts $d$ and $\operatorname{next}(d)$ lie in the same cycle of the strand traversal permutation of $D$, the permutation of the darts of $D$ that sends each dart $e$ to…
nodes.title: A traversal step stays in its strand cycle

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and let $a$ be a parameter point of $L$, given by a component $i$ and a parameter $t$. The projected tangent vector of $L$ at $a$ is the vector of $\mathbb{R}^2$ obtained by applying the standard projection $(x, y, z) \mapsto (x, y)$ to the derivative $\gamma_i'(t)$ of the curve $\gamma_i$ of the $i$-th component of $L$ at $t$.
nodes.title: Projected tangent vector

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of this projection. Then the under-strand preimage of $p$ and the over-strand preimage of $p$ are distinct parameter points of $L$.
nodes.title: Over and under preimages differ

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of this projection. The under-strand preimage of $p$ is the unique parameter point $a$ of $L$ that projects to $p$ and whose height is strictly less than the height of every other parameter point projecting to $p$; the height of a parameter point is the third coordinate of the corresponding point of $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
nodes.title: Under-strand preimage of a crossing
Topology

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
